<explanation>
1. Project Type and Purpose  
   - Airweave is a self-hosted, full-stack context-retrieval platform for AI agents.  
   - It comprises:  
     • A React/TypeScript frontend (dashboard/UI)  
     • A FastAPI Python backend (REST API + business logic)  
     • Supporting microservices/workers (Temporal workflows, Redis pub/sub)  
     • Data stores (PostgreSQL for metadata, Qdrant for vector embeddings)  
     • An optional MCP server (Node.js) and a connector toolkit (Monke)

2. High-Level Architecture Components  
   a. Frontend  
      - React/TypeScript app served via Docker (port 8080)  
      - Connects to backend REST API for user actions, visualization, and live API docs  
   b. Backend API  
      - FastAPI service (port 8001)  
      - Exposes v1 endpoints: collections, source connections, sync, search, billing, auth  
      - Implements business logic layers (core/, crud/, schemas/, search/, billing/, analytics/)  
   c. Worker/Orchestration Layer  
      - Temporal workers execute long-running sync workflows  
      - Redis for pub/sub (sync triggers, rate limiting, context caching)  
   d. Data Stores  
      - PostgreSQL: metadata tables (collections, users, auth, sync jobs) managed via Alembic  
      - Qdrant: vector store for semantic embeddings  
   e. External Integrations  
      - “platform/sources” connectors for 30+ apps (Slack, GitHub, Google Drive, etc.)  
      - “integrations” clients (Stripe, Auth0)  
      - Entity extraction, chunking, embedding using embedders (OpenAI, FastEmbed)  
   f. SDKs & MCP  
      - Python/TS SDKs wrap REST calls  
      - MCP microservice (Node.js) offers an alternative GraphQL-like interface  
   g. Monke  
      - Connector-generation CLI/framework (Python + its own frontend/backend)  

3. Interactions and Data Flow  
   1. User → Frontend (HTTP) → Backend API  
   2. Backend API → PostgreSQL (CRUD) for metadata  
   3. Backend API triggers syncs → Redis pub/sub → Temporal workflows  
   4. Workflows fetch data via connectors → chunk/transform → embed → store in Qdrant  
   5. User/API queries → Backend search service → Qdrant ● optional reranking → return results  
   6. SDKs or MCP server also consume the same API or directly interface with the backend  

4. Architectural Patterns & Principles  
   - Layered architecture: UI / API / Business Logic / Data Access / Storage  
   - Micro-worker pattern: Temporal + Redis for async/background tasks  
   - Pluggable connectors: strategy pattern for sources, embedders, destinations  
   - Multi-tenant via OAuth2, API keys, and per-collection isolation  
   - Incremental sync via cursors, hashing, rate limiting  

5. Diagramming Guidelines  
   - Use distinct shapes/colors:  
     • Blue rectangles for services (Frontend, API, MCP, Monke)  
     • Green cylinders for data stores (PostgreSQL, Qdrant, Redis)  
     • Orange hexagons for workers/orchestrators (Temporal)  
     • Grey clouds for external systems (Apps, SDK consumers)  
   - Label arrows with protocols or actions (HTTP, gRPC, Pub/Sub, CLI)  
   - Show clustering: group all “platform/sources” under one connector block  
   - Reduce whitespace:  
     • Place components in tight swimlanes  
     • Minimize margins around nodes  
     • Use smaller fonts and iconography to shrink overall footprint  
   - Keep the diagram compact:  
     • Align related components vertically/horizontally  
     • Collapse repetitive elements (e.g., multiple connectors) into a single “30+ Connectors” box  

6. Tailoring for Airweave  
   - Emphasize frontend ↔ API separation and ports (8080 vs. 8001)  
   - Highlight Temporal worker cluster connecting via Redis  
   - Show dual data stores: metadata vs. vector store  
   - Include SDK and MCP as alternate ingress points  
   - Optionally depict Monke as a separate CLI/service for connector generation  

7. Elements to Include  
   - Clear labels: service names, ports, DB types  
   - Directional arrows: data flow and dependencies  
   - Color coding/shapes: distinguish service, store, worker, external  
   - Reduced whitespace and tighter grouping for a smaller, denser diagram  

By following these guidelines, you’ll produce a precise, compact system diagram that captures Airweave’s layered architecture, async workflows, and pluggable connector ecosystem—all in a visually concise format.  
</explanation>
